sector: Stockbroking, dealing and foreign exchange (securities brokerage and market making)
howTheBusinessMakesMoney: Brokers earn a fee on every client order, win or lose: a commission per trade, a small spread on currency and bonds, interest on idle client cash and the firm's own capital held in treasury bills, and fees for placing bills and bonds. Market makers earn a tiny spread on huge volume while keeping their own positions small and hedged. Trading the firm's own money is a minor, tightly limited line. Regulators require locked capital, clean client files and fast settlement.

caseStudies.scale: 2025: net revenue above $6bn, commissions $2.1bn, net interest $3.6bn, 77% pretax margin, about 4m trades a day in Q4
caseStudies.lesson: Automation keeps cost low and the risk system closes positions that break limits with no human override. Copy: a Head of Risk who auto-closes at the limit, and income from fees plus interest, not bets.

caseStudies.scale: 2025: about $12.2bn trading revenue and about $6.5bn EBITDA, a record year for the market maker
caseStudies.lesson: Market makers earn a fraction of a cent on millions of orders and hold positions for seconds. Copy: earn the spread on client flow, keep inventory small, never bet the firm on one direction.

caseStudies.scale: 2025: top NGX broker by value, N2.18trn traded, 18.3% of the N11.94trn market total
caseStudies.lesson: Scale comes from big institutional tickets (pension funds, asset managers). Copy: a messenger van of bulk fund orders that pays a lower rate but huge volume once the firm is trusted.

caseStudies.scale: 2025: third on NGX by value, N735.5bn traded, 6.16% of market value
caseStudies.lesson: A bank-group broker wins on trust, compliance and access to pension and bank clients. Copy: clean files and a strong compliance desk unlock the biggest clients, not promises of return.

regulation.rule: Minimum capital to hold a licence
regulation.unitedStates: SEC Rule 15c3-1 net capital: $250,000 for firms holding client assets, $100,000 for dealers; FINRA membership required
regulation.nigeria: SEC Nigeria Jan 2026: N600m broker, N1bn dealer, N2bn broker-dealer, deadline June 30, 2027

regulation.unitedStates: SEC Rule 17a-11: notify the regulator when net capital falls below 120% of the minimum
regulation.nigeria: SEC Nigeria requires capital kept at the minimum at all times and periodic returns; shortfall means sanction

regulation.unitedStates: Federal Reserve Reg T: borrow up to 50% to buy; FINRA Rule 4210: at least 25% equity maintenance
regulation.nigeria: SEC Nigeria and CBN margin rules: separate margin accounts, 120% maintenance, bank exposure capped

regulation.unitedStates: SEC moved US equities to T+1 in May 2024; DTCC settles
regulation.nigeria: SEC Nigeria: T+2 from Nov 28, 2025, then T+1 from June 1, 2026 via CSCS

regulation.unitedStates: SEC-approved Limit Up-Limit Down bands pause trading in a stock moving too fast; no fixed daily cap
regulation.nigeria: NGX caps each share's daily move at plus or minus 10%; new volume thresholds for price change from 2026

regulation.unitedStates: SEC Rules 606/607 disclose payment for order flow; FINRA Rule 5310 requires best execution
regulation.nigeria: NGX dealing member rules: best price for clients, no front running; payment for order flow not used

regulation.unitedStates: CFTC and NFA regulate retail forex dealers; FinCEN registration for money services businesses
regulation.nigeria: CBN: BDC Tier 1 N2bn, Tier 2 N500m capital; sell at most 1% over purchase rate; $25,000 weekly cap

gameRules.name: Fees come first
gameRules.rule: fee = ticketValue x rate, paid whatever the price does. Shares 1.35% (0.75% at 5-star loyalty), T-bills 0.125%, bonds 0.10%, commodities 0.5%. Currency: sell at buyRate x 1.01 max.
gameRules.playerFeels: Steady, earned income from serving clients well
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Nigerian broker commission up to 1.35%; CBN 1% BDC margin cap; fee-led US brokers

gameRules.name: Own-book cap
gameRules.rule: Own trading unlocks at stage 4. Total own positions <= 10% of freeCash; any one position <= 2% of freeCash. freeCash excludes locked capital. Orders above the cap are refused with a reason.
gameRules.playerFeels: Trading is a small side dish, never the meal
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Dealer position limits and value-at-risk limits set by a risk officer

gameRules.name: Forced stop-loss
gameRules.rule: Any own position at -8% from entry closes automatically at the next tick. Worst day = 10% x 8% = 0.8% of freeCash. No override, no adding to a losing position.
gameRules.playerFeels: Losses are small, capped and over fast
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Automatic liquidation at broker risk systems (IBKR) and desk stop-loss limits

gameRules.name: No borrowing to trade
gameRules.rule: Own-book buy allowed only if cost <= settled freeCash. No margin loans for the firm or clients in game. Credit line, if any, may pay salaries only, never positions.
gameRules.playerFeels: You cannot dig a hole deeper than your own pocket
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Reg T, FINRA 4210 and Nigerian margin rules, made stricter for the game

gameRules.name: Clue-driven prices
gameRules.rule: Each day 3 clues each worth -3% to +3%. Move = sum of clues + noise in -1% to +1%, capped at -10% / +10%. Reading 2 of 3 right gives about +3% to +6%. No jackpot payouts.
gameRules.playerFeels: Reading the news matters more than luck
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: NGX plus or minus 10% daily price band; prices follow results, oil and inflation

gameRules.name: Locked capital vault
gameRules.rule: Licence capital is locked: N600m (stage 3), N1bn (4), N2bn (5+). It earns 15.4%/yr = 1.28% per game month. If it falls below 120% of required, own book freezes and warning shows.
gameRules.playerFeels: Safety money that still works quietly
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: SEC Nigeria 2026 capital tiers, SEC 17a-11 120% early warning, 91-day bill at 15.40%

gameRules.name: T+1 settlement
gameRules.rule: Fees credit 1 game day after the trade once the slip reaches the settlement counter. A ticket with wrong details fails: redo it and pay N10,000. 98% clean tickets for 30 days = 5-star rating.
gameRules.playerFeels: Accuracy pays; sloppy work costs money and stars
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Nigeria T+1 from June 2026 via CSCS; US T+1 since May 2024; failed-trade penalties

gameRules.name: Every loss explained
gameRules.rule: Each closed loss opens a recap card: entry, exit, loss in naira and % of freeCash, which clue was misread, and today's fee income beside it. Card must be read before the next own trade.
gameRules.playerFeels: I know exactly why I lost and how small it was
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Desk post-trade reviews and daily risk reports

stages.licenceOrGate: Rent a counter in a family member's licensed bureau de change; pass ID check
Pass stockbroker exams; sign with a sponsoring licensed broker; 40-client book
Broker licence: N600m capital locked, compliance officer hired, files inspected
Dealer licence: capital raised to N1bn; risk limits panel switched on
Broker-dealer licence: capital N2bn; 5-star rating; head of settlement
Pass regulator audit with zero missing client files; hire Head of Risk
Foreign licence and separate local capital for Johannesburg desk; one group risk limit
Licences in London, Dubai, New York; 24 months with no risk breach

uniqueMechanics.name: Ticket to settlement relay
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Carries order tickets from the client desk to the right dealing desk, then trade slips to the settlement counter before the T+1 cut-off. Wrong desk or wrong details means a failed trade.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Floor view with ticket tray, five desk stations, settlement counter and a T+1 countdown on each slip

uniqueMechanics.name: Morning clue board
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Reads 3 analyst clues each morning, then may place a few small own-book trades inside the 10% and 2% caps, or park cash in treasury bills instead.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Clue board with 3 cards, own-book panel showing cap bars, stop-loss lines and a T-bill option

uniqueMechanics.name: Capital vault and licence
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Locks licence capital in the vault, watches it earn bill interest, and keeps it above 120% of the requirement to climb the licence ladder.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Vault screen with locked capital, required level, 120% warning line and next licence target

failureStates.trigger: Locked capital under 100% of the required amount for 5 game days
failureStates.consequence: Licence suspended: own book closed, only client orders via a sponsor at half fees
failureStates.recovery: Top up capital from profits or an investor; regulator review takes 7 game days

failureStates.trigger: More than 5% of tickets fail settlement in a game week
failureStates.consequence: Star rating drops 2 levels; client arrivals fall 40% for 14 days
failureStates.recovery: Hire a settlement clerk or buy the Auto-Settlement Engine; 10 clean days restore 1 star

failureStates.trigger: Inspection finds missing client ID papers on over 2% of files
failureStates.consequence: Fine of 2% of monthly revenue and new clients paused for 3 days
failureStates.recovery: Compliance officer re-checks all files; next clean inspection lifts the pause

failureStates.trigger: A dealer event tries to double a losing position past the 2% cap
failureStates.consequence: Head of Risk blocks it; if no Head of Risk yet, a 1% of freeCash loss and a recap card
failureStates.recovery: Hire or train a Head of Risk; breach events stop for 30 days

balanceNotes: Target payback on spend (locked capital excluded since it is kept and earns interest): stages 1-2 about 2-6 months, stage 3 about 12 months, 4 about 10, 5 about 9, 6 about 3, 7 about 8, 8 about 10. Players will feel stuck saving N600m for the broker licence; ease it with an investor event and T-bill income. Tune first: share order arrival rate and the commission rate, then own-book clue payoff so it stays under 15% of total profit.
openQuestions: Nigeria moved to T+1 in June 2026: switch the storyline's two-day settlement to one day, or keep T+2 as a simpler early-game rule?
Should currency desk margin use the strict 1% CBN cap (small income) or a generic 1.5% for gameplay feel?
Is own-book trading allowed to show any loss larger than 1% of freeCash in a day, or is 0.8% the hard ceiling?
Should foreign desks (Johannesburg, London, Dubai, New York) use real-world named regulators in game text or generic ones?
